edges.effect_quant: The timing signal is directionally consistent but still rests mostly on surrogate cardiovascular outcomes rather than hard event reduction. In ELITE, estradiol started within 6 years of menopause slowed carotid intima-media thickness progression from 0.0078 to 0.0044 mm per year, whereas starting at least 10 years after menopause showed no benefit and numerically worse progression (0.0088 vs 0.0100 mm per year).
edges.population: postmenopausal women considering menopausal hormone therapy, with cardiovascular effects varying by age and years since menopause
edges.mechanism: Vascular responsiveness to estrogen appears to depend on how advanced the arterial substrate already is at the time therapy begins. Earlier after menopause, estrogen may preserve endothelial function and slow atherosclerotic remodeling, whereas later initiation may fail to help once plaque biology and vascular stiffness are already established.
edges.summary: The best-supported interpretation is not simply beneficial or harmful, but timing-dependent. Data from ELITE, KEEPS, and age-stratified interpretations of large hormone-therapy trials suggest that menopausal hormone therapy started close to menopause may have neutral-to-favorable vascular effects, while later initiation loses that advantage and may shift toward harm or no benefit.
edges.caveats: This edge relies heavily on subclinical atherosclerosis outcomes and secondary analyses rather than definitive reductions in myocardial infarction or stroke. Formulation, route, concomitant progestogen, baseline vascular health, and time since menopause all influence the result, so this should not be generalized into a simple 'HRT is cardioprotective' claim.

evidence.citation: Hodis HN et al 2016 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Vascular Effects of Early versus Late Postmenopausal Treatment with Estradiol.

effect_quant.comparator: annual carotid intima-media thickness progression with estradiol versus placebo among women less than 6 years since menopause (0.0044 vs 0.0078 mm per year); no benefit was seen in women 10 or more years since menopause

evidence.citation: ElKhoudary SR et al 2019 J Am Heart Assoc
evidence.notes: Effects of Hormone Therapy on Heart Fat and Coronary Artery Calcification Progression: Secondary Analysis From the KEEPS Trial.

effect_quant.comparator: any increase in epicardial adipose tissue with oral conjugated equine estrogens versus placebo in recently menopausal women

evidence.citation: Harman SM et al 2011 Am J Med
evidence.notes: Timing and duration of menopausal hormone treatment may affect cardiovascular outcomes.
